analysis.title: AI delivers despite volatility (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: Nasdaq futures pointed 1.2% lower ahead of the Thursday US open after Alphabet fell almost 10% after-hours on Wednesday and Samsung Electronics slid over 4% following results.

Alphabet's September-quarter sales from most core businesses came in below market expectations. Samsung's chip operations missed estimates, capex expanded, and details of a new shareholder return plan were delayed until the end of January.

Offsetting the misses, Alphabet's cloud revenue growth accelerated, Samsung posted record quarterly profit nearly nine times a year earlier, Microsoft's Azure exceeded expectations, and Oracle beat on both top and bottom lines.
UBS reads the reaction as elevated expectations going into reporting season and a sharper investor focus on AI monetization. Amazon's results due later Thursday are another catalyst.
UBS says recent tech results reinforce its view that AI fundamentals remain robust and support its constructive outlook on the AI trade.

Cloud growth acceleration: Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y (82% prior quarter, 34% in the March quarter), Azure +48% (43% in the June quarter), Oracle cloud growth 62% (from 47%). All three guided to further cloud growth, with added capacity supporting pipeline demand.

AI product monetization: Microsoft reported an eight-fold increase in large Copilot accounts and Alphabet said Gemini reached 1 billion users. A leading AI lab reported compute costs below 60% of revenue and enterprise AI spending under 1% of customers' total expenses.

Microsoft cut 2026 capex guidance slightly from USD 175bn to USD 170bn but said investment will accelerate next year. With Meta's equity raise and Alphabet's signal of significantly higher 2027 capex, UBS expects AI capex growth to keep benefiting quality semiconductor and hardware names.
Funding pressure and execution risk at specialized AI cloud providers warrant caution, but rising GPU rental prices point to robust demand for AI compute amid supply constraints.

UBS sees opportunities in hyperscalers and high-quality semiconductor and hardware companies, and advises managing concentrated positions via defensive tech areas and diversification across sectors and regions. Investors able to bear the risk can use structured strategies with capital preservation or yield features.

The Fed held rates at 3.75-4% on Wednesday as expected. The statement upgraded growth to 'strong' from 'solid' and two policymakers dissented in favor of a 25bp hike. The press conference was more dovish than the statement.

Chair Kevin Warsh cited improvement in inflation compensation and expectations and tighter financial and credit conditions since September. His remark that conditions are tighter but he is 'unwilling and unable to call them tight' suggests to UBS that the tightening cycle is not over. Market reaction was muted.

UBS expects 25bp Fed hikes in both December and March, versus three hikes priced by markets over the next 12 months. It reads Warsh as signaling gradual tightening, constructive for equities, fixed income and gold. Fewer FOMC meetings in 2027 and 2028 carry no clear policy implication to UBS.

UBS expects the ECB to hold on Thursday, with focus on its response to sovereign spread widening. A signal from Lagarde of willingness to counter spreads would likely support the euro. UBS's base case is EURUSD recovering toward 1.16 by year-end, and it likes selling the downside for yield pickup.

UK Chancellor John Healey's budget offers targeted cost-of-living relief (GBP 100 payment for up to 20 million households, extended VAT cut on electricity, removal of gas standing charges, fuel-duty freeze) funded partly by raising the Bank Corporation Tax Surcharge from 3% to 6% for 15 months and two percentage points more on savings and property income tax rates.
OBR forecasts UK GDP growth of 1.2% this year, 1% next year and 1.6% in 2028, with borrowing falling from 4.2% of GDP to 1.8% by 2030-31 and GBP 15bn of headroom.

UBS sees limited effect on UK growth and inflation, a muted gilt reaction, and a persistent UK risk premium in longer-dated yields from fiscal credibility concerns. It stays constructive on sterling against the Swiss franc, says the UK bank surcharge is manageable, and continues to like European bank stocks.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell almost 10% after hours on Wednesday as September-quarter sales from most core businesses missed expectations, though cloud revenue growth accelerated to 103% y/y.
Azure exceeded expectations with 48% growth, and large Copilot accounts rose eight-fold. 2026 capex guidance was trimmed to USD 170bn from USD 175bn, with investment to accelerate next year.
Beat estimates on both revenue and earnings, with cloud growth quickening to 62% from 47%.
Results due later Thursday are flagged as another catalyst for the AI trade.

sector_views.sector: Technology (AI hyperscalers, quality semiconductors and hardware)
sector_views.rationale: AI fundamentals remain robust, cloud growth is accelerating and AI capex should keep supporting the compute complex. UBS advises managing concentration by adding defensive tech and diversifying.
Earnings story is broadening beyond rates to loan growth, Europe's capex cycle, fee income and wealth management, and AI-driven efficiencies.

earnings_insights: Alphabet (reported Wednesday after the close, September quarter): sales from most core businesses below market expectations, Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y vs +82% prior quarter and +34% in the March quarter. Shares fell almost 10% after hours.

Samsung Electronics (reported, September quarter): chip operations missed estimates, capex expanded, record quarterly profit nearly nine times a year earlier, shareholder return plan details delayed until end of January. Shares fell over 4%.
Microsoft (reported): Azure +48% for the three months to September vs +43% in the June quarter, above expectations. 2026 capex guidance cut to USD 170bn from USD 175bn.
Oracle (reported): beat estimates on revenue and earnings, cloud growth 62% vs 47% prior quarter.
Amazon results are due later on Thursday 29 October.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Held unchanged as expected, with two dissents favoring a 25bp hike and the growth assessment upgraded to 'strong'.
Markets price three hikes over the next 12 months. UBS expects gradual tightening, which it views as constructive for equities, fixed income and gold.
Recovery depends partly on the ECB signaling willingness to counter sovereign spread widening.
UBS expects limited effect from the budget on growth and inflation.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GBP 15bn of fiscal headroom, with tightening back-loaded around the next general election, which keeps a risk premium in long gilts.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth accelerated at Alphabet (103%), Azure (48%) and Oracle (62%), Copilot and Gemini show monetization, and capex is set to rise in 2027, supporting hyperscalers and quality semiconductors.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated expectations drove an almost 10% after-hours drop in Alphabet on core-business sales misses, and funding pressure and execution risk at specialized AI cloud providers warrant caution.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that cloud growth and AI monetization stop accelerating, or that capex guidance is cut materially rather than trimmed (Microsoft's cut was USD 175bn to USD 170bn with acceleration promised).

tension_points.bull_case: Warsh's press conference was more dovish than the statement and pointed to a gradual path, which UBS says is constructive for equities, fixed income and gold.
tension_points.bear_case: The statement upgraded growth to 'strong', two policymakers dissented for a hike, and Warsh's 'unwilling and unable to call them tight' remark suggests tightening is not over. Markets price three hikes versus UBS's two.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A shift to an accelerated hiking pace rather than the gradual 25bp steps UBS expects in December and March.
